target.title: refactor(qa): retire the standalone Matrix QA runtime
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Matrix release QA had two independently maintained execution systems: the QA Lab scenario host and a standalone `qa-matrix` plugin with its own runtime, catalog, profiles, artifacts, retries, and workflow jobs. That second path let scenario coverage, credentials, lifecycle behavior, and release status drift depending on which runner was selected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Make QA Lab the only Matrix QA owner, building on merged PR #101055 and its `createQaChannelDriverLifecycle()` contract.

- Removes the `extensions/qa-matrix` package/plugin, registrations, dependencies, private runtime/catalog, Matrix-only artifacts, and standalone release orchestration.
- Keeps `pnpm openclaw qa matrix` only as a thin QA Lab selector for the shared scenario/profile host and selected Matrix transport adapter.
- Represents migrated Matrix behavior as ordinary QA Lab `kind: flow` scenarios. A compact `flow.module` / `flow.call` declaration becomes a shared QA Lab flow step; there is no Matrix fixture API or adapter-owned scenario runner.
- Uses the selected adapter only for lifecycle and flow preparation. `live:matrix` prepares the live Matrix scenario context and `crabline:matrix` remains selectable for portable flows through the same QA Lab execution path.
- Keeps scenario selection, sequencing, retries, timeouts, assertions, artifacts, and failure reporting in QA Lab instead of the transport adapter.
- Maps all 94 historical scenario IDs: 81 keep same-ID module-backed flows and 13 renamed IDs map to maintained QA Lab scenarios.

No compatibility fallback is retained because it would recreate a second Matrix execution path.

## User Impact

Maintainers and release managers get one Matrix QA implementation and evidence format.

- `qa matrix --profile release` remains the focused two-scenario release selector.
- `qa matrix --profile fast` retains 11 scenarios.
- `qa matrix --profile transport` retains 50 scenarios.
- Media and E2EE profiles retain their previous membership.
- `qa matrix` / `--profile all` retains the 92-scenario default profile, with two legacy explicit-only scenarios still excluded from the default exactly as before.
- Per-scenario provider mode, Matrix config, retry count, timeout, artifacts, and failure semantics are preserved.

There is no shipped Matrix channel runtime change. Packaged OpenClaw releases continue to omit private QA Lab tooling.

## Evidence

- Architecture and migration parity:
  - PR #101055 is merged; its channel-driver lifecycle seam remains the only live Matrix lifecycle path.
  - No `fixtureApi`, top-level `fixture:` scenario field, Matrix scenario executor, adapter `runScenario`, private catalog, or compatibility fallback remains.
  - The 94-entry migration proof resolves 81 same-ID module-backed scenarios plus 13 renamed mappings with no missing or duplicate IDs.
  - Profile assertions: `all=92`, `fast=11`, `release=2`, `transport=50`, `media=7`, `e2ee-smoke=8`, `e2ee-deep=18`, `e2ee-cli=9`.
- Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox:
  - `tbx_01kwyj4z2n1y4msce7qajwdavb` (`golden-hermit`): 125 focused SDK/QA Lab tests passed; 29 Matrix observer/topology tests passed.
  - `tbx_01kx19kc03v216415p5v8hqfpe` (`jade-hermit`): final focused SDK/QA Lab proof passed, 96 tests total.
  - `tbx_01kx1b1pg1258tbx0x2rg3c8p4` (`pearl-crab`): targeted oxlint, dependency analysis, `check:test-types`, private-QA build, and both live/Crabline Matrix lifecycle tests passed.
  - `git diff --check` passed.
- Review:
  - Fresh whole-branch Codex autoreview on `6d741482a9e163b7f42b630deaa99a8c34590ec4`: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- Exact-head GitHub proof:
  - CI and ClawSweeper dispatch started automatically for `6d741482a9e163b7f42b630deaa99a8c34590ec4`.
  - Focused `qa-live-matrix` release proof: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28961936962
  - Full manual QA Live proof: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28961938624
